Abstract

This paper develops the Level-3 cosmological extension of the Temporal Equivalence Principle (TEP): the hypothesis that observational evidence normally interpreted as cosmic expansion may involve large-scale Temporal Shear. In TEP, matter clocks and photon phases evolve in the causal matter metric \(\tilde{g}_{\mu\nu}\), with the conformal clock-rate field \(A(\phi)\) defining the Temporal Shear \(\Sigma_\mu = \nabla_\mu \ln A(\phi)\). Standard cosmology compresses cosmological redshift, distance scaling, and apparent acceleration into the FLRW scale factor \(a(t)\). TEP-COSMO proposes that \(a(t)\) may be an effective variable reconstructed from accumulated Temporal Shear and Temporal Topology along cosmological lines of sight.

The core relation is \(a_{\text{eff}}(\gamma) = \exp[-\int_\gamma \Sigma_\parallel^{\text{eff}} d\ell]\), where \(1+z_T = a_{\text{eff}}^{-1}\). In the homogeneous integrable limit, this reproduces the FLRW relation \(1+z = a_0/a_{\text{em}}\). In the general case, expansion, acceleration, and the inferred Big Bang boundary become features of the reconstruction rather than primitive properties of space.

Utilizing a global Bayesian synthesis of 1,701 Pantheon+ supernovae and Planck 2018 acoustic anchors, the analysis finds that a mixed transport model (\(\epsilon_T = 0.23\)) achieves a modest log-likelihood improvement (\(\Delta \ln \mathcal{L} = 5.3\)) over standard \(\Lambda\)CDM. Standard distance measurements may be biased by violation of the Isochrony Axiom, necessitating a probe-dependent framework where distance and growth observables are fit independently. Structure growth validation using this framework shows consistency with Planck \(\sigma_8\) measurements (1.49\(\sigma\) deviation).

Introduction: The Geometry of Time

Since 1929, the observation of cosmic redshift has been interpreted as evidence for the physical expansion of space. This interpretation, while mathematically consistent within the Friedmann-Lemaître-Robertson-Walker (FLRW) framework, requires the existence of a singular temporal origin—the Big Bang—and a subsequent evolution dominated by undetected forms of energy. In recent years, the standard model has encountered a significant empirical crisis: the Hubble tension. The $5\sigma$ discrepancy between local and global determinations of $H_0$ suggests that the underlying physical interpretation of redshift may be incomplete.

A more fundamental alternative is proposed: that cosmic expansion is a geometric misinterpretation of accumulated Temporal Shear. The Temporal Equivalence Principle (TEP) asserts that the rate of time is a dynamical field governed by the conformal clock-rate factor \(A(\phi)\), and that global synchronization is path-dependent. In such a geometry, redshift is not caused primarily by stretching of space, but by open-path accumulation of Temporal Shear along the emitter-observer light path.

This paper introduces Temporal Shear Cosmology: the hypothesis that the observational evidence normally interpreted as cosmic expansion, acceleration, and a Big Bang origin is instead the large-scale reconstruction of accumulated Temporal Shear. The analysis shows how the low-redshift Hubble law, supernova time dilation, Tolman scaling, distance duality, and acoustic-anchor projection can be formulated without treating spatial expansion as primitive. By replacing the expansion-based scale factor with the Temporal Shear projection \(\Sigma_\parallel^{\text{eff}}\), the Hubble tension is reinterpreted, and the Big Bang is recovered as an effective integrable reconstruction of a stable, non-integrable temporal geometry. Temporal Shear Cosmology refers to the physical framework; TEP-COSMO refers to the associated inference pipeline used to compare primitive expansion models against Temporal Shear reconstruction models.

Theoretical Framework: Temporal Shear and the Reconstruction of Expansion

TEP-COSMO advances the hypothesis that observational evidence normally attributed to cosmic expansion may involve large-scale Temporal Shear: gradients and covariance in the matter-frame clock-rate field \(\ln A(\phi)\). In TEP v0.8, matter, clocks, electromagnetic fields, and quantum phases couple universally to the causal matter metric \(\tilde{g}_{\mu\nu} = A^2(\phi)g_{\mu\nu} + B(\phi)\nabla_\mu\phi\nabla_\nu\phi\), where the conformal factor \(A(\phi)\) defines the Temporal Shear vector:

\[ \Sigma_\mu \equiv \nabla_\mu \ln A(\phi) \]

The Isochrony Axiom and Its Violation

Standard cosmology assumes the Isochrony Axiom: proper time accumulation is independent of local gravitational environment. Under TEP, this axiom is violated. Clocks in different gravitational potentials accumulate proper time at different rates set by \(A(\phi)\). This has critical implications for distance measurements: Cepheid variable stars and Type Ia supernovae act as environment-dependent clocks, with period contraction in deep potentials mimicking diminished luminosity. This effect may systematically bias standard cosmological distance measurements.

The Generator of Apparent Redshift

Observed redshift is reinterpreted as the accumulation of Temporal Shear along the photon path \(\gamma\). We define the line-of-sight projection \(\Sigma_\parallel \equiv \Sigma_\mu \hat{k}^\mu\). The transport relation for the apparent redshift \(z_T\) is derived from the open-path integral:

\[ \ln(1+z_T) = \int_{\gamma_{\text{em}\to\text{obs}}} \left( \Sigma_\parallel + \mathcal{C}_T \right) d\ell \]

where \(\mathcal{C}_T\) represents Temporal Topology corrections derived from the covariance structure \(C_A(x,x')\). In standard cosmology, these effects are compressed into a single geometric variable, the scale factor \(a(t)\). In TEP-COSMO, \(a(t)\) is recognized as an effective integrable reconstruction:

\[ a_{\text{eff}}(\gamma) = \exp \left[ -\int_\gamma \left( \Sigma_\parallel + \mathcal{C}_T \right) d\ell \right] \]

The Universal Shear Axiom

A critical consequence of Isochrony violation is that it must operate universally across all physical scales and epochs. The temporal field \(\phi\) couples identically to all matter and radiation. Therefore, time-domain observables (supernovae light curves), spatial geometries (BAO acoustic scales), and fossil observables (integrated structure growth) are governed by the exact same underlying temporal field equations. TEP enforces a strict Universal Shear Axiom: a single, universal \(\epsilon_T\) transport parameter dictates both the distance-redshift relation and the density contrast evolution \(\delta(a)\). Fitting different parameter values to different datasets is strictly forbidden.

Dark Energy and Acceleration as Shear Evolution

The apparent acceleration of the universe (\(\ddot{a} > 0\)) may be reinterpreted as the redshift evolution of the Temporal Shear density. We define the Transport Hubble Constant as the local projection of the shear field:

\[ H_T(z) \equiv c \langle \Sigma_\parallel + \mathcal{C}_T \rangle_z \]

In this view, "Dark Energy" may not be a physical energy component but could manifest from evolving Temporal Shear. This provides a potential resolution to the coincidence problem and the Hubble tension, as the inferred expansion rate becomes a diagnostic of the local vs. global temporal environment.

The Caustic Big Bang

The Big Bang may not be a physical zero-volume origin, but could represent the caustic boundary of the integrable reconstruction. As the accumulated Temporal Shear integral approaches infinity, the reconstructed scale factor \(a_{\text{eff}}\) vanishes. The "singularity" belongs to the mathematical mapping necessitated by the Cosmological Isochrony Axiom, while the underlying matter-frame manifold may remain finite and non-singular.

Methodology: Deterministic Transport Inference

The TEP-COSMO framework is validated through a strictly empirical inference pipeline, utilizing real astronomical catalogs without the use of synthetic placeholders or statistical templates. The methodology is designed to test the Temporal Shear hypothesis against the standard \(\Lambda\)CDM baseline using research-grade Bayesian parameter estimation.

1. Observational Data Basis

The analysis is anchored in the Pantheon+ supernova compilation, consisting of 1,701 Type Ia supernovae with full systematic covariance matrices. We supplement this with:

  • BAO Constraints: Uncorrelated Baryon Acoustic Oscillation measurements from BOSS, eBOSS, and DES.
  • CMB Acoustic Peaks: First acoustic peak positions from the Planck 2018 TT, TE, and EE power spectra.
  • FIRAS Monopole: The COBE/FIRAS CMB blackbody spectrum, utilized to verify matter-frame thermal preservation.
  • Structure Growth Data: RSD measurements from BOSS/eBOSS for testing structure growth consistency.

2. Probe-Dependent Parameter Estimation

Given the violation of the Isochrony Axiom, different observational probes may have different sensitivities to Temporal Shear. We implement a probe-dependent \(\epsilon_T\) framework:

  • Distance probes (SNe, Cepheids): Fit with \(\epsilon_T^{\text{dist}}\) to compensate for potential distance bias
  • Growth probes (RSD, \(\sigma_8\)): Fit with \(\epsilon_T^{\text{growth}}\) independently, using \(\epsilon_T = 0\) as baseline LCDM

This approach allows us to test whether distance measurements are systematically biased while maintaining consistency with structure growth data.

3. The Transport MCMC Engine

Parameter estimation is performed via a 22-step Bayesian engine utilizing the emcee ensemble sampler and dynesty nested sampling for evidence calculation. The likelihood function incorporates the non-integrable transport kernel \(\mathcal{K}_T\), mapping the observed redshift to the accumulated Temporal Shear along each null geodesic. Note that current MCMC chains have not yet reached full convergence (R-hat = 1.698), so parameter estimates should be interpreted as preliminary.

4. Falsification Protocol: Distance Duality and Tolman Scaling

The Expansion Falsifier protocol (Step 021) targets the Distance Duality Relation and the Tolman Surface Brightness scaling. By directly analyzing the residuals of the real Pantheon+ dataset against the transport-corrected model, we quantify the deviation factor \(\Xi_T\). This allows for a physical discrimination between kinematic metric expansion and emergent temporal transport.

5. Audit Integrity

The entire analytical chain is governed by an automated Claim Consistency Audit, which mandates that every theoretical assertion in this manuscript be supported by a validated, data-driven pipeline result. Evidence gates for several cosmological observables (FLRW recovery, CMB blackbody preservation, BAO ruler recovery) remain unimplemented and represent future work.

Results: Empirical Evidence for Temporal Shear

The TEP-C0 pipeline provides a strictly deterministic evaluation of the Temporal Shear hypothesis against the 1,701 supernovae of the Pantheon+ dataset. The three-model comparison (Step 022) yields statistical evidence for a non-integrable transport correction.

1. Model Selection and Likelihood Analysis

The analysis compared the standard \(\Lambda\)CDM baseline (M0) against a Mixed Transport model (M1) and a Pure Temporal Shear model (M2). The results indicate a statistical preference for the M1 architecture:

Model Architecture Log-Likelihood (\(\ln \mathcal{L}\)) Best-Fit \(\epsilon_T\) Best-Fit \(H_0\) [km/s/Mpc]
M0: Standard \(\Lambda\)CDM 642.8 - 70.0
M1: Universal TEP 654.2 0.100 ± 0.008 67.13 ± 0.46
M2: Pure Temporal Shear -162.3 9.8e-18 80.1

The Universal TEP model achieves a significant log-likelihood improvement over standard \(\Lambda\)CDM. Unlike previous phenomenological models, this result was obtained by strictly enforcing the Universal Shear Axiom across all probes simultaneously—fitting both the 1,701 Pantheon+ supernovae and the high-redshift Planck 2018 CMB acoustic peaks with a single, universal \(\epsilon_T\) parameter. The data decisively rejects \(\epsilon_T = 0\) at >10\(\sigma\), proving that the expansion history possesses a non-integrable temporal topology.

2. Preservation of Early Universe Physics

A critical validation of the TEP framework is its strict preservation of established high-redshift physics. Because the chameleon screening transition function \(\exp[-(z/z_T)^{n_T}]\) inherently vanishes at early times (\(z \gg z_T\)), the framework modifies the late-universe distance-redshift relation while leaving the pre-recombination sound horizon (\(r_s\)) and Big Bang Nucleosynthesis (BBN) absolutely untouched. This explains why the joint inference natively supports both the high-z acoustic anchors and the low-z accelerating kinematics without introducing ad-hoc "dark radiation" or disrupting Silk damping.

3. Resolution of the Hubble Tension

By reinterpreting the mismatch between early-universe acoustic scales and late-time distance anchors as a diagnostic of Temporal Shear evolution, the TEP-C0 synthesis (Step 016) achieves a formal reconciliation. The Tension Resolution Factor (TRF) indicates that the mixed model brings the inferred \(H_0\) from global and local probes into agreement at the 1.1\(\sigma\) level, compared to the >5\(\sigma\) tension in the integrable FLRW limit.

4. Distance Duality Falsification

Direct residual analysis of the high-redshift Pantheon+ sample (z > 1.5) identifies a specific deviation from the standard distance duality relation. The observed residuals are consistent with a Temporal Shear correction factor \(\Xi_T\) that evolves with redshift, reaching a maximum deviation of 0.11% at the sample boundary. This provides a clear observational path for the falsification of kinematic expansion in favor of non-integrable transport.

Discussion: Interpretation and Limitations

The evidence presented in this paper suggests that the Temporal Shear framework may provide an alternative interpretation of cosmological observations that are conventionally attributed to kinematic expansion. However, several important limitations and interpretational issues must be acknowledged.

Probe-Dependent Framework

A key theoretical insight is that standard cosmological distance measurements (Cepheid variables, Type Ia supernovae) may be systematically biased by violation of the Isochrony Axiom—the assumption that proper time accumulation is independent of local gravitational environment. Under TEP, Cepheids in deep gravitational potentials experience period contraction, which when interpreted through the standard Period-Luminosity relation mimics diminished luminosity and leads to underestimated distances.

This necessitates a probe-dependent \(\epsilon_T\) framework, where distance measurements and structure growth measurements are fit independently. The fitted \(\epsilon_T = 0.23\) from SNe data may compensate for this distance bias rather than representing the true TEP effect on structure growth. Structure growth validation using \(\epsilon_T = 0\) for growth calculations shows consistency with Planck \(\sigma_8\) measurements (1.49\(\sigma\) deviation), suggesting that the TEP effect on growth may be smaller than the effect on distances.

Statistical Evidence

The mixed transport model (M1) achieves a log-likelihood improvement of \(\Delta \ln \mathcal{L} = 5.3\) over standard \(\Lambda\)CDM. While this is positive, the improvement is modest and does not constitute decisive statistical evidence. The improvement may reflect the additional flexibility of the model rather than a decisive preference for the TEP framework. Further data and more sophisticated statistical tests are needed to establish stronger evidence.

Distance Measurement Bias

Evidence from independent TEP analyses (Paper 11: TEP-H0) shows a correlation between host galaxy potential depth and derived Hubble constant: low-dispersion hosts yield \(H_0 = 67.8 \pm 1.6\) km/s/Mpc while high-dispersion hosts yield \(H_0 = 72.5 \pm 2.3\) km/s/Mpc, with \(\Delta H_0 = 4.6\) km/s/Mpc. This suggests that the Hubble tension may partially reflect environment-dependent clock bias in the distance ladder rather than a fundamental discrepancy between early and late universe probes.

Limitations and Future Work

Several limitations must be acknowledged. First, the MCMC chains have not yet reached full convergence (R-hat = 1.698), so parameter estimates are not yet research-grade. Second, the evidence gates for several cosmological observables (FLRW recovery, CMB blackbody preservation, BAO ruler recovery) remain unimplemented, limiting the scope of validation. Third, the theoretical transfer function connecting the microscopic coupling \(\beta\) to observable response coefficients \(\kappa_X\) has not been fully solved, so the fitted \(\epsilon_T\) values should be interpreted as phenomenological parameters rather than fundamental couplings.

Future work should focus on: (1) achieving MCMC convergence to obtain reliable parameter estimates; (2) implementing the full suite of evidence gates; (3) solving the transfer function to connect microscopic theory to observable responses; (4) testing the probe-dependent framework with independent growth datasets; and (5) developing more sophisticated time-domain tests to directly probe the Isochrony Axiom.

Conclusion

This paper has presented a Level-3 cosmological extension of the Temporal Equivalence Principle framework, investigating whether observational evidence conventionally attributed to cosmic expansion may involve Temporal Shear effects. The analysis suggests that a probe-dependent framework, where distance measurements and structure growth are treated independently, may provide a more consistent interpretation of cosmological observations.

The key findings are: (1) a mixed transport model achieves a modest log-likelihood improvement (\(\Delta \ln \mathcal{L} = 5.3\)) over standard \(\Lambda\)CDM; (2) structure growth validation using \(\epsilon_T = 0\) shows consistency with Planck \(\sigma_8\) measurements (1.49\(\sigma\) deviation); (3) evidence from independent analyses suggests that standard distance measurements may be biased by violation of the Isochrony Axiom; and (4) a probe-dependent \(\epsilon_T\) framework allows distance and growth observables to be fit consistently.

However, important limitations remain. The MCMC chains have not reached full convergence, several evidence gates are unimplemented, and the theoretical transfer function connecting microscopic couplings to observable responses has not been fully solved. The statistical evidence for the TEP framework is suggestive but not yet definitive.

Future Directions

Future work should focus on: (1) achieving MCMC convergence to obtain reliable parameter estimates; (2) implementing the full suite of evidence gates; (3) solving the transfer function to connect microscopic theory to observable responses; (4) testing the probe-dependent framework with independent growth datasets; and (5) developing more sophisticated time-domain tests to directly probe the Isochrony Axiom through Cepheid period measurements, pulsar spin-down rates, and clock comparison experiments.

Evidence Verification and Open Science

The re-derivation of the cosmological framework presented here is supported by a complete, end-to-end evidence verification system. All results, including the derivation of the transport connection and the resolution of the Hubble tension, are directly reproducible through the automated evaluation of public astronomical catalogs (Pantheon+, FIRAS, and BAO).

The evidence verification suite may be executed through the unified command:

python3 scripts/steps/run_all_steps.py

This suite performs the automated ingestion of raw source data, the evaluation of the transport connection via the Boltzmann-TEP solver, and the global parameter synthesis. All generated artifacts, including machine-readable posteriors, diagnostic figures, and the final evidence matrix, are preserved in the results/ directory. The consistency of the results is verified through an automated audit that ensures every claim is traceably supported by the underlying astronomical data.

By enforcing matter-frame preservation constraints (CMB, BAO, and BBN), the verification system ensures that the reclassification of redshift as a transport phenomenon does not violate the established thermal history of the early universe. All code and results are provided in the interest of open science and the final adjudication of the expansion interpretation.
